ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit-length $\lambda$ and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}$ ' and put in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}^{\prime}$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1 \mathrm{~m}, \lambda=1 \Omega / \mathrm{m}, \omega=2 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ and $B=1 \mathrm{~T}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a bent rigid thin wire frame, with vertices M, N, P, P', N', M' marked. The right side NPP'N' is a square, and the left side MNN'M' is another square. The two squares are bent along the direction where NN' lies into two mutually perpendicular planes. The green dashed line indicates that the rotation axis passes through NN', with angular velocity ω. The red arrow indicates the magnetic field B, whose direction is perpendicular to NN'. Reasoning: According to the specified method, regard MNPP'N'M' as a closed 6-segment wire loop, with total length 6L, so the total resistance R=6λL. Let the rotation angle θ=ωt. The normal vectors of the two squares differ by 90°, so the magnetic flux through the right square can be written as BL^2 cosθ, and the magnetic flux through the left square can be written as BL^2 sinθ. The total magnetic flux is Φ=BL^2(cosθ+sinθ), and the sign convention does not affect the heat. The magnitude of the induced electromotive force satisfies E=|dΦ/dt|=BL^2ω|cosθ−sinθ|. The time average of E^2 over one revolution is B^2L^4ω^2, because the period average of (cosθ−sinθ)^2 is 1. The period for each revolution is T=2π/ω, so the heat released Q=∫E^2/R dt=(B^2L^4ω^2/R)(2π/ω). Substituting L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s, R=6 Ω, gives Q=(1·1·(2π)^2/6)·(2π/(2π))=2π^2/3≈6.58 J.

raw_record.question_text: Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit length $\lambda$, and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}'$ and put in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}'$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1\,\mathrm{m}$, $\lambda=1\,\Omega/\mathrm{m}$, $\omega=2\pi\,\mathrm{rad/s}$, and $B=1\,\mathrm{T}$.

method.method_draft: Use Faraday flux for the whole bent closed wire. From the image, treat MNPP'N'M' as one closed 6-segment loop folded into two perpendicular square faces, with fold/axis NN'. Let the magnetic flux through the right square be B L^2 cos(theta) and through the left square be B L^2 sin(theta), because the two square normals are 90 degrees out of phase as the frame rotates. Thus total flux can be written Phi(theta)=B L^2[cos(theta)+sin(theta)] up to an irrelevant sign convention, with theta=omega t. The induced emf is |E|=|dPhi/dt|=B L^2 omega |cos(theta)-sin(theta)|, whose squared time average over one revolution is B^2 L^4 omega^2. The total wire length is 6L, so the resistance is R=6 lambda L. The heat per revolution is Q= integral over one period of E^2/R dt = (B^2 L^4 omega^2/R)(2 pi/omega). Substitute L=1, lambda=1, B=1, omega=2 pi to get Q=2 pi^2/3≈6.58 J.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个弯折的刚性细导线框，标出顶点 M、N、P、P'、N'、M'。右侧 NPP'N' 是一个正方形，左侧 MNN'M' 是另一个正方形，两正方形沿 NN' 所在方向折成互相垂直的两个面。绿色虚线表示转轴通过 NN'，角速度为 ω。红色箭头表示磁场 B，方向垂直于 NN'。

推理：按指定方法，把 MNPP'N'M' 视为一个闭合的 6 段导线回路，总长度为 6L，因此总电阻 R=6λL。设转角 θ=ωt。两个正方形的法向量相差 90°，所以穿过右侧正方形的磁通可写为 BL^2 cosθ，穿过左侧正方形的磁通可写为 BL^2 sinθ。总磁通为 Φ=BL^2(cosθ+sinθ)，符号约定不影响热量。感应电动势大小满足 E=|dΦ/dt|=BL^2ω|cosθ−sinθ|。一周内 E^2 的时间平均值为 B^2L^4ω^2，因为 (cosθ−sinθ)^2 的周期平均值为 1。每转一周周期 T=2π/ω，所以放热 Q=∫E^2/R dt=(B^2L^4ω^2/R)(2π/ω)。代入 L=1 m，λ=1 Ω/m，B=1 T，ω=2π rad/s，R=6 Ω，得 Q=(1·1·(2π)^2/6)·(2π/(2π))=2π^2/3≈6.58 J。

method.method_draft: Compute the motional emf directly from the moving wire: E= contour integral of (v x B) dot dl. Choose the rotation axis NN' as z. The two radial directions from NN' to PP' and MM' are perpendicular unit vectors e1(theta) and e2(theta), rotating with theta=omega t. For a point at radius r, v=omega zhat x r. In a uniform B perpendicular to z, (v x B) is parallel to the axis, so the four radial top/bottom edges give zero contribution because dl is radial. Only the two vertical outer edges PP' and MM' contribute; their axial line integrals give an emf proportional to B omega L^2 times the sum/difference of the projections of e1 and e2 onto B, i.e. E(theta)=B omega L^2[cos(theta)-sin(theta)] up to sign. Therefore the mean square emf over a full revolution is B^2 omega^2 L^4. The loop resistance is six edges times lambda L, R=6 lambda L. Then Q per revolution is integral E(theta)^2/R dt from 0 to 2pi/omega, giving Q=pi B^2 L^3 omega/(3 lambda)=6.58 J for the given values.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中导线框由两个边长为 L 的正方形组成，右侧正方形为 NPP'N'，左侧正方形为 MNN'M'，二者共用竖直边 NN' 且所在平面互相垂直。绿色虚线表示转轴通过 NN'，角速度为 ω。红色箭头表示磁场 B，方向垂直于 NN'。

推理：按指定方法，用运动电动势公式 E=∮(v×B)·dl。取转轴 NN' 为 z 轴。两块方框从轴向外伸出的径向单位矢量分别为 e1(θ) 和 e2(θ)，且二者互相垂直并随 θ=ωt 转动。距离转轴半径为 r 的点速度为 v=ω zhat×r。因为 B 垂直于 z 轴，所以 v×B 沿轴向，因此径向边上的 dl 为径向，贡献为零；只有两条外侧竖直边 PP' 和 MM' 对回路电动势有贡献。由两条外侧竖直边的轴向积分可得瞬时电动势大小可写为 E(θ)=BωL^2[cosθ−sinθ]，符号不影响发热。一个周期内的均方值为 <E^2>=B^2ω^2L^4，因为 <(cosθ−sinθ)^2>=1。整条闭合导线框有 6 条边，每条边长 L，单位长度电阻为 λ，所以总电阻 R=6λL。每转一周释放的热量 Q=∫0^(2π/ω) E^2/R dt = (B^2ω^2L^4)/(6λL)·(2π/ω)=πB^2L^3ω/(3λ)。代入 L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s，得到 Q=π·1·1^3·2π/(3·1)=2π^2/3≈6.58 J。

raw_record.original_question: Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit length $\lambda$, and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}'$ and put in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}'$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1\,\mathrm{m}$, $\lambda=1\,\Omega/\mathrm{m}$, $\omega=2\pi\,\mathrm{rad/s}$, and $B=1\,\mathrm{T}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows a bent rigid thin wire frame, with vertices M, N, P, P', N', M' marked. The right side NPP'N' is a square, and the left side MNN'M' is another square. The two squares are bent along the direction where NN' lies into two mutually perpendicular planes. The green dashed line indicates that the rotation axis passes through NN', with angular velocity ω. The red arrow indicates the magnetic field B, whose direction is perpendicular to NN'.

Reasoning: According to the specified method, regard MNPP'N'M' as a closed 6-segment wire loop, with total length 6L, so the total resistance R=6λL. Let the rotation angle θ=ωt. The normal vectors of the two squares differ by 90°, so the magnetic flux through the right square can be written as BL^2 cosθ, and the magnetic flux through the left square can be written as BL^2 sinθ. The total magnetic flux is Φ=BL^2(cosθ+sinθ), and the sign convention does not affect the heat. The magnitude of the induced electromotive force satisfies E=|dΦ/dt|=BL^2ω|cosθ−sinθ|. The time average of E^2 over one revolution is B^2L^4ω^2, because the period average of (cosθ−sinθ)^2 is 1. The period for each revolution is T=2π/ω, so the heat released Q=∫E^2/R dt=(B^2L^4ω^2/R)(2π/ω). Substituting L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s, R=6 Ω, gives Q=(1·1·(2π)^2/6)·(2π/(2π))=2π^2/3≈6.58 J.
